title: Sequential PLC crane automation
summary: Mode management, sequence control and interlocks for a two-axis crane moving between treatment tanks.
objective: Coordinate horizontal and vertical crane motion through initialization, manual, assisted and automatic modes in an academic industrial-process model.
work: Define the operating modes and their transition conditions.
Structure GRAFCET sequences and modular control logic.
Validate tank and height setpoints before executing motion.
Use operator feedback and interlocks to clarify the current machine state.
outcome: The team report preserves program organization, selection blocks, timing logic and setpoint validation. Handwritten GRAFCET material supplements the report figures.
limits: This case study describes the academic implementation documented by the team. The native PLC and HMI project exports are not included, and the website does not connect to a live machine.
sources: ELE8202 project 1 team report and archived GRAFCET sheets. Figures are report excerpts, not a live PLC session.

title: STM32 musical game
summary: An embedded note game combining a display, timing, communication and audio output.
objective: Coordinate game state, note timing, score and display updates on an STM32-based hardware setup.
work: Organize note and game-state handling in C.
Integrate an ILI9341 display with the microcontroller peripherals.
Use UART, timers and audio-related interfaces in the application.
Document the wiring and prototype assembly.
outcome: The archive includes application source, an IOC configuration, a Keil project and a two-page wiring and montage PDF. The gallery recovers the actual hardware photographs from that PDF.
limits: The firmware has not been rebuilt for this portfolio. The team demonstration link is provided as an external reference rather than a claim that the website emulates the game.
sources: Project wiring and montage PDF; main.c and guitar.c in the archived STM32 project.

title: Mechanical chess board
summary: An 8 x 8 sensing board, LED feedback and three-axis motion with an electromagnet.
objective: Develop a physical board capable of supporting a solo chess experience through sensing, game logic and mechanical movement.
work: Specify occupied-square sensing with magnetic sensors.
Break down sensing, display and motion into functional modules.
Explore shift-register inputs and LED-matrix output.
Prepare board layouts and mechanical models for the proposed mechanism.
outcome: The original Wokwi sketch combines eight input registers for 64 sensors, LED-matrix updates, chess-engine calls and three-axis motor commands. The archived diagrams and mechanical files document the wider design.
limits: This animation is a visual positioning model, not an Arduino firmware emulator or a reproduction of the original Micro-Max engine. Hardware accuracy, collision clearance and full autonomous operation have not been independently validated here.
sources: Original Wokwi control sketch, functional specifications, board diagrams and archived Arduino input-register tests. The source sketch identifies the inherited chess engine separately from the sensor, display and motor-control work.

title: Odroid C2 Linux build environment

Separate build configuration from generated target images.
Document the boundary between the operating-system build and the application.

limits: The final camera-security application source was not identified. Buildroot, a completed QR reader and a fully reproducible application release are not claimed by this case study.
sources: Archived meta-ele4205 layer configuration and Odroid C2 build artifacts. The cover is a typeset excerpt of a real file, not a fabricated IDE screenshot.

title: Arc-flash and protection study
summary: Arc-current inputs, incident-energy calculations and time-current protection curves.
objective: Examine how fault conditions, electrode configurations and protection clearing times affect an academic arc-flash calculation.
work: Organize equipment input parameters and fault cases.
Read the relationship between fault current and clearing time on TCC plots.
Compare how protection assumptions change calculated exposure.
Document assumptions and calculation boundaries.
outcome: The report contains input and result tables, and the archive preserves a set of annotated TCC plots. The gallery presents these as saved coursework evidence.
limits: These are academic calculations, not an approved safety assessment. They must not be used to select PPE, authorize energized work or establish safe operating procedures for a real installation.
sources: Team report and saved TCC plots.

title: Nonlinear loads and transformers
summary: LED-load measurements, waveform distortion and three-phase transformer configurations.
objective: Investigate the electrical behavior of nonlinear lighting loads and compare transformer connections in a reduced laboratory setup.
work: Characterize current and voltage waveforms for the tested loads.
Record power and harmonic quantities with laboratory instruments.
Compare three-phase winding configurations.
Relate oscilloscope captures and instrument readings to the report calculations.
outcome: The archive preserves wiring diagrams, oscilloscope captures, harmonic tables, instrument photographs and silent measurement clips. These provide both the experimental context and the recorded outputs.
limits: Different saved configurations and draft summaries are not treated as a single validated dataset. The lighting installation in the assignment is a teaching scenario, not a building commissioned by the team. No guaranteed THD reduction is claimed here.
sources: ELE8458 TP3 part 1 report, saved transformer diagrams and instrument captures. Report excerpts are selected to omit team identifiers.

Keep calculation assumptions visible alongside the results.
outcome: The saved assignments contain calculation steps and circuit figures. Selected figures are presented as coursework examples rather than design packages for a real installation.

title: Signal analysis in Python
summary: Windowing, chirps, correlation and sampling explored through saved notebook outputs.
objective: Connect time-domain signal behavior to spectra, correlation and sampling effects.

Apply a Hamming window and inspect spectral changes.
Compare auto-correlation and cross-correlation in a radar-style exercise.
Explore aliasing and the interpretation of sampled spectra.
outcome: The PDF notebook exports preserve code, plots and written analysis. The gallery extracts the plots themselves, without the cover-page identifiers or grading material.
limits: These are saved notebook results, not newly executed simulations. The original notebooks and course black-box modules are not distributed here.
sources: ELE2700 TP3, TP4 and TP5 notebook PDF exports. Figure descriptions preserve the distinction between coursework and a deployed sensing system.

title: Communication and channel coding
summary: Signal analysis, Simulink models and a Hamming 7,4 decoding workflow.
objective: Explore a communication chain from signal generation and spectral inspection to block-code decoding.
work: Organize a Simulink signal-analysis model and setup parameters.
Prepare bit streams for block decoding.
Reshape received data into seven-bit words.
Use the Hamming decoder and reassemble the decoded bit stream.
outcome: The archive includes simulation models and MATLAB coding helpers. A selected diagram from the lab handout documents the intended signal-analysis setup; it is labeled as reference material rather than a completed experiment screenshot.
limits: The models and radio hardware have not been run for the portfolio. The decoding helper assumes the framing used by the original exercise, including its header length. It is not a general-purpose radio receiver.
sources: Archived MATLAB decoding helper and ELE3701A TP3 lab handout. Reference diagrams are identified as such.

limits: The archived numerical calculations have not been independently checked. The figures are coursework evidence, not an operational network study or an endorsed design recommendation.
